transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Sinha (Redwood SE), Daniel Rowe (CSM), Sam Park (SE), Jordan Lee (Cobalt Eng Manager), Mei Chen (Cobalt SRE), Tom Alvarez (CTO), Ravi Patel (Platform)

Summary:
Quick sync during POC stability sprint. Reviewed last week's stress run results, discussed autoscale thresholds and burst plans for Dedicated pool, agreed on runbook updates and next stress windows. Decided to run a fallback canary using smaller quantized model when KV cache warm-up misses exceed 15%. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Stress run readout (throughput, tail latency, KV cash hit rates)
- Autoscale policy tuning (headroom, cool-down, CPU/GPU metrics)
- Burst planning for reserved capacity and pre-warm slots
- Rollback/fallback model routing and canary test
- Security checklist & SOC2 items briefly touched

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, we want to keep this under an hour, quick recap from last run and then ops items.
[00:22] Jordan: yeah thanks Alex, we saw the 2 hour stress window last thursday, throughput climbed fine but tail latency spiked around minute 22 and again at 1:05. we captured traces.
[00:37] Priya: quick clarifying question — when you say tail latency, is that p95 or p99?
[00:43] Jordan: mostly p99, p95 also moved but p99 was the big concern.
[00:50] Mei: also the KV cash hit-rate fell from 92% to about 64% during the ramp, seems like cold prefixes were killing us.
[01:05] Alex: interesting, so two axes: cache warm-up and autoscale reaction. the dedicated pool should've autoscaled, did the HPA/LB trigger?
[01:18] Ravi: the k8s HPA did spin up nodes but there was a 45s queuing window before the new slices got warmed, we suspect the cold kv cache and model kv latch.
[01:35] Sam: note that our recommended autoscale policy uses token-backpressure plus GPU utilization and queue length, with a 30s cool-down by default. might need to shorten to 15s for this workload.
[01:50] Priya: and we can also add a pre-warm threshold — keep an extra 10% reserved instances during business hours to absorb spikes.
[02:05] Tom: cost sensitivity is real for us. if we bump reserved to 10% that increases monthly. can you quantify delta?
[02:15] Alex: we estimate a 7-12% increase in unit cost for steady state, but the tail latency improvement is significant — p99 down from 1.8s to 0.6s in our test.
[02:30] Jordan: those numbers sound good, but we need the exact math for finance.
[02:35] Daniel: we'll produce a brief cost/benefit spreadsheet, Alex will lead.
[02:48] [03:00] Priya: on fallback routing — we discussed using a smaller quantized variant as a graceful degradation. plan is: if KV hit < 75% and p99 > 1.2s then route new requests to model-xq-quant.
[03:20] Mei: caveat — model-xq-quant has different tokenization and sometimes changes output formatting; we need to flag downstream parsers.
[03:35] Jordan: oh that's important, our payments parser is strict. we cant allow format drift.
[03:43] Alex: agreed, so fallback must be limited to low-risk endpoints (post-auth analytics, not payment validation).
[03:55] Sam: or use fallback but attach a 'probability' header, so we can route 10% to fallback for canary flagging and compare outputs.
[04:10] Ravi: on the autoscale metrics side, we saw GPU util was a lagging indicator; queue depth and per-request token generation time gave earlier signals.
[04:25] Priya: yes we recommend combining queue depth, 1m moving avg of token time, and KV hit ratio as composite signal for scale-up.
[04:38] Jordan: can you share the exact PromQL rules so our SREs can mirror them?
[04:44] Priya: sure, we'll export the rules. expect them in the next day.
[04:55] [05:10] Mei: about burst planning — how many pre-warm GPU slots can Redwood reserve in Dedicated during a super-spike? we need 200 concurrent model slots for 10 minutes during a sale.
[05:25] Alex: we can reserve burst capacity up to agreed commit, but we also have a burst pool for transient spikes. for 200 concurrent slots, need to define model size; are we using 8-bit quant and 16k context?
[05:40] Jordan: we're running the 13B open variant with 8-bit inference, typical sequence length 512 tokens.
[05:50] Alex: ok, roughly each slot is ~7GB GPU memory; 200 slots is about 1.4TB worth — that maps to number of GPUs, we can provision but cost and time to spin up matters.
[06:05] Tom: what's the fastest we can spin that up?
[06:10] Alex: with pre-warmed instances it's immediate; cold provisioning is minutes to tens of minutes depending on region.
[06:18] Mei: last run the regional market had limited spare GPUs so cold spin-up failed to meet SLA.
[06:24] Alex: that's why we suggest a hybrid: small reserved baseline + burst pool for quick spillover + local pre-warm slices. Also a fallback to smaller model for immediate safety.
[06:38] [06:50] Jordan: ok, sounds like three levers: reserved baseline, pre-warm slots, model fallback. what about routing policy during failover?
[06:58] Priya: we support weighted routing across variants and region-level failover; policy can be based on token cost, latency SLO, or static priority.
[07:12] Ravi: we want region failover off by default because of data residency.
[07:18] Alex: understood, we'll keep region pinned unless explicit.
[07:22] [07:30] Sam: quick note on metrics — include prefix KV eviction count in dashboards. that helps debug warm-up holes.
[07:40] Mei: on the next run, we'll capture prefix distribution so we can simulate realistic cache warming.
[07:50] [08:05] Jordan: one of the strange things — when we dropped to smaller model, some entity extractions mis-labeled amounts. I'm worried about downstream regressions.
[08:18] Priya: that's expected; smaller quantized models can shift confidence. suggestion: use fallback only for non-critical paths and set a raised sampling rate to audit outputs.
[08:30] Alex: propose this run plan: 1) replicate last week's stress pattern but with a 15s autoscale cool-down, 2) reserve 8% pre-warm capacity during window, 3) enable 10% canary to fallback model to compare outputs, 4) capture KV hit metrics and traces.
[08:55] Tom: agree, also we need the security team to confirm that sampling doesn't leak PII when we sample outputs.
[09:05] Daniel: we will share a sanitized sampling config and redaction guidance.
[09:15] [09:30] Priya: actionables — I'll push the PromQL, Alex will update runbook and cost spreadsheet, Mei will run the controlled test.
[09:40] Jordan: question — if we shorten cool-down to 15s won't we have thrash (scale up then down repeatedly)?
[09:50] Sam: to prevent thrash, use asymmetric cool-downs: short scale-up (15s) and longer cool-down (60-90s) for scale-down. also require sustained queue depth above threshold for 10s before scale-up.
[10:10] Mei: that sounds reasonable. we'll also add a minimum replica floor so we never go under baseline.
[10:20] [10:35] Jordan: what about prewarming KV cache? can Redwood prepopulate prefixes before a sale?
[10:45] Priya: yes we can push a warm-up job that issues synthetic prefixes to populate KV. that should run ~10-15 minutes before expected spike.
[10:58] Ravi: is that safe with live traffic? it will increase request volume.
[11:05] Alex: it's intended to be internal warm calls and limited to private VPC network, won't touch customer data — we'll use synthetic payloads that mimic shapes, not real PII.
[11:18] Tom: fine, security will want a runbook and approval flow.
[11:25] [11:40] Priya: small note on monitoring — we'll add a regression alert when canary disagreement rate exceeds 2% for payment-critical endpoints.
[11:50] Mei: ok and we'll attach that to a page channel for on-call.
[12:00] [12:15] Jordan: final item — can you provide a short playbook for manual failover? our on-call might need to flip routing quickly.
[12:25] Alex: yes, we'll add a one-page ops runbook with steps: 1) enable fallback routing, 2) increase reserved pre-warm, 3) trigger warm job, 4) notify stakeholders.
[12:36] Priya: I'll draft the canary config and the PromQL this afternoon.
[12:44] Alex: noted. any other questions?
[12:50] Tom: not from me. thanks everyone.
[12:55] Alex: recap of next steps and owners, thanks all — we'll reconvene after the two runs next week.

Action items (re-iterated):
- Alex Moreno: update runbook + cost spreadsheet, share by 2025-06-20
